species: mouse (Thy1-ChR2, nNOS-ChR2 transgenic and non-transgenic control lines)
readout_other: Local field potential (LFP) recordings in motor cortex via chronic tungsten electrode, evoked by ultrasound and optogenetic (ChR2) stimulation of somatosensory barrel cortex
direction_notes: Ultrasound stimulation of somatosensory barrel cortex evoked a negative LFP deflection in motor cortex (indicative of depolarization) similar in polarity/timing to optogenetic activation of cortical pyramidal (excitatory) neurons, but 10- to 20-fold smaller in amplitude; the evoked response required living tissue and did not attenuate over a 10-min stimulation period.

exposures.label: Ultrasound stimulation of somatosensory barrel cortex

timing.protocol_description: A TTL trigger triggered waveform generator 1 to undergo a square wave train of 10 ms duration (the ultrasound stimulus train). During each 10 ms stimulus train, waveform generator 1 produced twenty square pulsed waves (each of 0.5 ms duration) with a 50% duty cycle (2.0 kHz repetition), and at the onset of each of these 20 pulses waveform generator 2 triggered the transducer to emit 75 acoustic cycles at 350 kHz (~0.214 ms per ultrasound event). Stimulation events (10 ms stimulus trains) were delivered at 7 Hz throughout the duration of the ten-minute recordings; craniotomy-based transdural stimulation was delivered to the somatosensory barrel cortex with LFP recorded in monosynaptically-connected motor cortex.

Time zero is the time of stimulus onset. P values are the effect of time on potential. Inset in B shows equivalent optogenetic stimulation data from mice not expressing ChR2 (n = 5).

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: At the onset of each of these 20 square pulsed waves, waveform generator 2 triggered the transducer to undergo 75 acoustic cycles at an acoustic frequency of 350 kHz (yielding an ultrasound event duration of approximately 0.214 ms).

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: The duty cycle for these 350 kHz ultrasound events was thus (0.214 ms)/(0.5 ms) 100%= 42.8%.
